messages:
Sam W.: heads up — since the rack network firmware rollout in eu-west1c we've got a bunch of GPU jobs stuck in Pending and a couple nodes showing huge egress queuing. noticed this at ~07:15 UTC when batch inference slowness spiked
Maya P.: saw that too, started getting alerts for pod startup >10m. any errors in the scheduler logs?
Leo R.: digging now. my first pass: k8s reports normal allocatable GPUs but our rack-level egress shaping is dropping bursts, kube-proxy conntrack is spiking which seems to delay kubelet heartbeats -> late node status updates -> pods linger in scheduling.
Irene O.: can you paste the pod describe? which error?
Leo R.: sure, short extract: ```
Name:           embedder-job-92
Namespace:      ml-batch
Status:         Pending
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled         18m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ml-batch/embedder-job-92 to node-rack3-gpu-07
  Warning  FailedScheduling  17m   default-scheduler  0/8 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient cpu, 5 Insufficient memory.
  Normal   BackoffLimitExceeded 5m  job-controller      Job has reached the specified backoff limit
```
(not super clean, but shows scheduling churn)
Sam W.: sounds like we have transient resource accounting mismatches due to delayed node updates rather than real GPU shortage. but some pods are actually ending up orphaned on nodes with degraded NICs and then getting evicted.
Maya P.: i pushed a quick probe to check node Ready timing and conntrack counts: ```kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.conditions[-1:].type,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp``` doesn't show much. but `ss -s` on affected hosts shows TCP: timewait and orphaned sockets huge.
Irene O.: temporary mitigations? can we taint the flaky nodes as network-unhealthy so scheduler avoids them while we rollback firmware?
Leo R.: yes. propose: add taint `network/egress=degraded:NoSchedule` on nodes with egress queues > threshold, then create a toleration patch for low-priority infra jobs we want to keep. also flip scheduler predicate to prefer spread over strict binpack for the next 30m to avoid concentrating retries onto same nodes.
Sam W.: +1. runbook step?
Irene O.: I'll coordinate with infra for the rollback window. steps: 1) mark nodes `cordon` those with >90% egress qlen 2) apply taint 3) drain non-stateful pods with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` 4) set scheduler rollout flag `prefer_soft_spread=true` in canary for 30m 5) monitor job queue and costs
Maya P.: doing step 1/2 now on rack3 nodes: `kubectl cordon node-rack3-gpu-0{5..8}` and `kubectl taint nodes node-rack3-gpu-05 network/egress=degraded:NoSchedule`
k8s-bot: note — node-rack3-gpu-06 cordoned by Maya P. at 2026-03-20T07:42:10Z
Sam W.: quick note on cost: if we start spreading to other AZs we'll pay cross-az egress and higher spot churn. prefer rollback if infra can do it fast.
Leo R.: agree. i'll also patch the scheduler to lower the binpack scoring weight for 30m (`--scoring-weight=soft_spread:0.7,binpack:0.3`) and roll it in canary. will post diff in a sec.
Maya P.: after taint/cordon drains started, some pods rescheduled to warm nodes in eu-west1b, latency back to normal for a subset. but a few long-running jobs hit BackoffLimit. we'll need to reconcile logs for the failed ones.
Irene O.: infra rollback scheduled in 22m. if that succeeds we'll un-taint and uncordon, then run a gentle rebalance to consolidate GPUs back (to avoid multi-az egress for long jobs).
Sam W.: thanks all. keep updates here. if rollback slips >30m escalate to oncall pager. :thumbsup:
Irene O.: update — rollback started at 07:58 UTC, monitoring egress qlen. initial signs promising, queue dropping on node-rack3-gpu-07.
Leo R.: scheduler canary applied. scoring change diff: `- binpack:1.0` -> `+ binpack:0.3; soft_spread:0.7`
Maya P.: requeues reduced, jobs finishing. will follow up with postmortem note (short) and a recommended preflight for future firmware rollouts to include rack egress soak test.
Sam W.: perfect. postmortem please include: 1) why conntrack spike correlated with firmware change, 2) why scheduler didn't avoid concentrating retries, 3) proposed preflight tests. closing thread after PM posted.
